messages:
maya: Quick sync — we need to decide scope/prioritization for JSON mode + schema validation. Customer asks are split: enterprise wants strict enforcement, PLG wants forgiving UX. Options: strict reject, auto-repair+retry, or best-effort. Thoughts?

sam: From runtime POV: strict validation on the response path forces buffering and kills streaming (or adds incremental validation complexity). Expect ~20–50ms overhead if we validate post-hoc.

nish: ML note — models frequently flip types or drop keys. Repair (re-prompt) helps but costs extra tokens and is nondeterministic. We should measure token cost for retries.

olivia: Sales: banking customers will accept extra latency for guaranteed conformance; they'd likely pay/commit to Dedicated/Private for that. PLG users prefer default repair to avoid noisy failures.

maya: High level tradeoffs: a) strict -> clear failure semantics, simpler billing; b) auto-repair -> better UX but extra cost/complexity; c) in-band streaming + validation -> hardest. We need launch criteria and API surface decisions (flags, headers, SDK ergonomics).

sam: Engineering proposal: make default = best-effort parse + one automatic repair attempt. Add an opt-in flag header `Validate: strict` that enforces strict semantics (no streaming, return 400 + validation errors). Also expose `max_retries` and `retry_mode` options in request JSON.

nish: Suggest we add `schema_version` header to route prompt templates and collect targeted evals. Retry modes: `repair` (attempt to fix) vs `reroll` (new generation). Each has different cost profiles.

olivia: OK from GTM: map `Validate: strict` to Dedicated/Private GA and keep `repair` default for Hosted. Make pricing notes in the PRD (retry token charge visible).

sam: Implementation details: add a validation hook in the serving runtime. If `Validate: strict` -> buffer output until EOS and run validator; on failure return structured error. If default -> stream tokens but run final validator; on fail, run a repair prompt flow once and stream final result (mark that it was repaired). We'll add metrics for retry_count, repair_success_rate, and extra_tokens_consumed.

maya: Proposed launch criteria: 1) Validator supports JSON Schema draft-07 for GA. 2) Repair template achieves >=90% pass rate on our eval corpus. 3) SDK flags and docs shipped. 4) Telemetry and cost dashboard for retries.

nish: Eval plan: gather prompt sets from 10 pilot customers + synthetic edge cases (nested arrays, optional keys, type coercion). Also add fuzz tests and adversarial prompts.

olivia: Docs + examples needed. Sample request for strict mode and sample 400 body: 
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
Headers: Authorization: Bearer $KEY, Validate: strict, Schema-Version: v1
Body: {"model":"rwd-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Give me a JSON matching the schema"}],"max_tokens":512}
```
Error (400):
```json
{ "error":"validation_failed", "details": ["missing key: transactions", "field amount expected number but got string"] }
```

sam: We'll also expose SDK-level helpers: `client.chat.create({..., validate: 'repair' | 'strict', schema: {...}})` so customers can pass inline schema for quick tests.

ops-bot: Created issue #987: "json-mode retry policy and strict validation flag" assigned to sam, ETA 2w.

maya: Great — can we aim to finalize decisions by EOD Friday? I'll draft the PRD and rollout plan and include the GA vs Hosted defaults. :thumbsup:
